amendments.change: (a) Judge A (Claude) now runs via the Message Batches API (50% cheaper; non-latency-sensitive batch job) — identical prompts/rubric/model, no scoring change. (b) Added a THIRD independent judge, Judge C = Meta Llama 4 Scout Vision (local MLX; fallback Llama-3.2-11B-Vision), so reliability triangulates across three model families (Anthropic/Qwen/Meta) instead of two. (c) Inter-rater reliability generalized from a single Cohen's weighted kappa to the MEAN of pairwise weighted kappa across present judges; the pre-registered endpoint (composite_weighted_kappa, threshold 0.4) is unchanged in name/meaning and reduces to the old two-judge number when only two judges are present.
amendments.why_still_confirmatory: Committed before any analyzed generation run (only a 2-image pipeline smoke test had been executed). Methodology §4: a pre-data methods change stays confirmatory; documented here as a dated amendment rather than a silent rewrite. Fields below still read 'two judges' in places — this amendment is authoritative where they differ.

derives_from.finding_being_hardened: Exploratory Kluver Level-2/3 dose-response (reduplication, fragmentation, condensation, distortion rise as guidance falls; SDXL distortion rho=-0.64, SD3.5 weaker). Currently fragile: single fixed prompt, single VLM judge, no inter-rater reliability, low-g confounded with under-conditioning, no multiple-comparison correction.
derives_from.what_this_adds: Turns that post-hoc exploratory signal into a pre-registered confirmatory result along four axes: (1) multi-prompt generality, (2) two independent judges + human-rated subset with inter-rater reliability, (3) quality-controlled guidance-matching to de-confound low-g breakdown from under-conditioning, (4) multiple-comparison correction.

anchor_papers: Kluver (1966), Mechanisms of Hallucinations -- Level-2 (polyopia/dysmegalopsia/dysmorphopsia) and Level-3 (spatio-temporal) constants; the taxonomy scored here.
Carhart-Harris & Friston (2019), REBUS and the Anarchic Brain -- precision-relaxation framing the guidance knob is the diffusion analogue of.

subquestions_addressed.Q1_existence: Does object-level breakdown (Kluver L2/3) appear as guidance falls, across a prompt set rather than one still life -- vs merely degrading to low-quality noise?
subquestions_addressed.Q3_dose_response: Is the L2/3 dose-response a graded curve that survives (a) prompt variation, (b) a second independent judge, and (c) controlling for image quality, so it is not just under-conditioning artifact?

hypothesis: When guidance g is lowered on SDXL and SD 3.5, holding prompt/seed/steps fixed, a composite objecthood-dissolution score (mean of z-scored Kluver Level-2/3 fields: reduplication, fragmentation, condensation, distortion) rises as g falls, and this rise (a) generalizes across a 6-prompt set spanning object count and objecthood, (b) survives correction for image quality -- i.e. is present after partialling out a no-reference quality score, so it is not merely under-conditioning -- and (c) is agreed on by two independent judges (Claude Sonnet 5 + open-weight Qwen2.5-VL-7B) at adequate inter-rater reliability.
null_result: Any of: (i) the composite guidance slope is flat (standardized LMM slope CI includes 0) on at least one model once pooled across prompts with random prompt/seed intercepts; (ii) the slope vanishes after partialling out image quality (quality-controlled partial Spearman |rho| < 0.1) -- meaning the Exp 01 signal was under-conditioning, not objecthood dissolution; (iii) the two judges do not agree (quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa on the composite fields < 0.4), rendering the metric uninterpretable (inconclusive-null). Each is a first-class reportable outcome: it would say the hardened finding does not hold.

prompts.text: a watermelon, a glass half-filled with water, and a set of keys on a wooden table

intended_inventory.note: one watermelon, one glass, one set of keys on a tabletop

prompts.text: a close-up portrait photograph of an elderly man's face
prompts.role: single organic object; acute distortion detector; clean reduplication-zero baseline

prompts.text: a red bicycle leaning against a brick wall
prompts.role: single rigid manufactured object; hard-edge geometry

prompts.text: a bowl of oranges on a kitchen counter
prompts.role: high natural multiplicity; tests reduplication BEYOND intended count and condensation

intended_inventory.distinct_objects: one bowl containing a plausible ~5-10 oranges
intended_inventory.note: reduplication scored only as multiplication implausibly beyond a normal bowl, or oranges appearing outside the bowl / tiling the frame

prompts.text: an empty living room with a sofa, a lamp, and a window

intended_inventory.note: one sofa, one lamp, one window in a coherent room

prompts.text: a forest of pine trees on a misty mountainside
prompts.role: low-objecthood control; should show tiling but LOW reduplication/condensation if the effect is object-bound

intended_inventory.note: reduplication baseline is high by design; score condensation/distortion of tree forms and tiling, not raw tree count

guidance_grid_rationale: 7-value subset spanning the inverted-U quality curve: low/under-conditioned arm (1,2,3), comfort-zone peak region for SDXL ~5-8 (5,7), and over-conditioned/oversaturated high arm (11,15). Both arms are required for the quality-matched two-arm contrast.

unconditional_baseline.note: empty-prompt baseline, prompt-independent, 10 seeds per model; anchors the true base layer as in Exp 01.

fixed.scheduler: model-default on MPS/CPU; DPM++ 2M Karras on CUDA only; SD 3.5 native flow-matching sampler
fixed.dtype: MPS: float32 for SDXL, float16 for SD 3.5; CUDA float16 (identical to Exp 01)

metric.name: composite_objecthood_dissolution
metric.per_image_per_field: mean over the two judges (Claude Sonnet 5, Qwen2.5-VL-7B) of the 0-3 ordinal score
metric.standardization: each field z-scored across all conditioned images WITHIN a model
metric.composite: per image, mean over the 4 z-scored fields
metric.primary_endpoint: the single composite per model (keeps the confirmatory family at 2 tests); the 4 individual fields are secondary.
metric.judge_gate: if quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa between the two judges on the composite fields < 0.4, the metric is deemed unreliable and the confirmatory claim is withheld (inconclusive-null).

primary_statistical_model.fit: per model (sdxl, sd35), on Judge-A+B mean composite
primary_statistical_model.guidance_std: z-scored guidance value (interval treatment, as Exp 01 treated the ordinal metric M)
primary_statistical_model.effect_of_interest: the guidance_std fixed-effect slope; negative slope = L2/3 rises as g falls
primary_statistical_model.why_lmm: random prompt intercept removes prompt-level baseline differences so the slope is the WITHIN-prompt guidance effect -- this correctly handles the high-baseline-multiplicity prompts (p4, p6). Random seed intercept absorbs per-seed variance.
primary_statistical_model.effect_size: standardized slope beta reported alongside p; effect estimation is primary per Methodology Section 5.

guidance_matching.purpose: De-confound the low-g effect from under-conditioning (SDXL g=1.0 is out of its comfort zone ~5-8, so breakdown there may be low-quality artifact rather than objecthood dissolution).

quality_metric.name: no_reference_image_quality
quality_metric.runs: local on M4, per image; no reference distribution needed; stable at per-bin N
quality_metric.curve: Q(model, g) = mean quality over prompts x seeds; g_star = argmax_g Q (per-model comfort-zone peak)
quality_metric.why_not_fid_or_clipscore: FID needs a reference set and hundreds of samples per bin to be unbiased (noisy at N~10); CLIP-score rises ~monotonically with g (measures prompt adherence, not quality) so its peak is just high-g -- wrong shape for a comfort zone.

primary_deconfound.test: partial Spearman correlation of composite vs guidance, controlling for Q
primary_deconfound.confirm_if: remains negative with |rho| >= 0.2 and bootstrap CI excludes 0
primary_deconfound.null_if: |rho| < 0.1 after controlling Q (the effect WAS under-conditioning)

secondary_contrast.test: matched-quality two-arm: quality is inverted-U, so a given Q level occurs at both a low-g and a high-g point. Compare composite at the low-g arm vs the quality-matched high-g arm.
secondary_contrast.interpretation: if low-g breakdown were generic quality loss, the oversaturated high-g point at matched Q would show similar composite. More L2/3 at the low arm = effect specific to the under-conditioning direction.
secondary_contrast.reported: Cliff's delta (low-arm vs quality-matched high-arm) with bootstrap CI
secondary_contrast.caveat: requires the two arms' quality ranges to overlap; if not, the partial correlation stands as primary and this is reported as not-computable.

full_set.multi_judge_method: per field, the reported weighted kappa is the MEAN of the pairwise weighted kappa across present judges (claude+qwen, claude+llama, qwen+llama); Gwet AC2 and percent agreement are likewise mean-of-pairwise. Reduces to the single pairwise value when only two judges are present (2026-07-21 amendment).
full_set.note: reported per field (ordinal 0-3) and for the composite; because several fields are 0-heavy (skewed marginals -> the kappa paradox), kappa is interpreted ALONGSIDE Gwet AC2 and percent agreement, not alone. Tiling (binary) uses unweighted kappa.

human_subset.sampling: stratified across (model x guidance-bin x prompt) so the subset spans the range
human_subset.rater: single human (author), blind, shuffled order, guidance hidden, identical rubric
human_subset.measures: human-vs-Claude and human-vs-Qwen quadratic-weighted kappa per field
human_subset.limitation_noted: single human rater -> reported as a limitation in analysis.md; no human-human reliability available.

calibration_cross_check.purpose: Judge A is Sonnet 5, not Exp 01's Sonnet 4.6 -- confirm the metric stays comparable to Exp 01.
calibration_cross_check.procedure: re-judge a fixed sample of existing Exp 01 images with Sonnet 5 on the (generalized) rubric; confirm the L2/3 field scores track the archived Sonnet 4.6 numbers (Spearman across images).

multiple_comparison_correction.primary_family: 2 tests (composite LMM slope, one per model) -- kept deliberately small so the headline claim is not multiplicity-inflated.
multiple_comparison_correction.secondary_family: 4 fields x 2 models = 8 field-level dose-response tests, corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg FDR; reported as q-values with standardized effect sizes (Methodology Section 5).

confirm.prompt_generality: guidance-slope sign consistent (negative) in at least 5 of 6 prompts per model in a per-prompt descriptive breakdown

samples.images_per_model: 6 prompts x 7 guidance x 10 seeds + 10 uncond = 430

budget.gpu: Apple M5 Pro 64GB (single primary host). 64GB unified memory runs SD 3.5 without cpu-offload/slicing and both judges locally; no sharding required (the 3x M4 24GB sharded path from Exp 01 remains available but is unnecessary here).

qwen.note: 7B is the pre-registered default (reproducible on modest hardware). On the 64GB host Qwen2.5-VL-32B (4-bit, ~20GB) runs without friction and is the drop-in fallback if 7B's human-subset kappa is poor; swapping the judge model does not change rubric_version.

llama.runtime: MLX on Apple Silicon (M5 Pro 64GB), mlx-vlm>=0.1.21
llama.note: Third judge / third model family (Meta). Latest Llama vision (17B active / 109B total MoE); 4-bit weights ~55GB are borderline on 64GB -- smoke-test load first. Drop-in fallback if it OOMs or mlx-vlm is too old: Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct-4bit (~7GB, dense). Pinned via EXP03_LLAMA_MODEL; swapping does not change rubric_version.

swappable_without_reclassifying: judge_models (rubric_version fixed; changing judge model does not change the scoring text)
